newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cutters say could process most diamonds.
newsitem.headline: Russian cutters say could process most diamonds.

text.p: Russia's diamond cutting industry can process $1 billion dollars worth of Russia's $1.3 billion annual output of rough diamonds, a top cutting industry executive said.

"Russian cutters can consume $1 billion of the $1.3 billion of rough diamonds mined," Yevgeny Bychkov, president of the Russian Diamond Cutters Association and former head of the disbanded State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones, said on Thursday.
"The remaining $300 million is not profitable for Russia to cut and can be sold, either on the (domestic) market that is being organised or to De Beers," he told a news conference.
Russia's Almazy-Rossii Sakha (ARS) produces nearly all of Russia's diamonds and had sales of $1.38 billion last year.

Bychkov said an export agreement with De Beers which has been awaiting Russian government approval for months was being looked at by President Boris Yeltsin's administration as well as the ministries of economy, finance, and foreign trade.
"I think it will somehow succeed this year," he said of the contract.

ARS and De Beers have been negotiating an export deal but the deal has been stalled in the Russian government and De Beers recently said it would terminate an interim agreement at the end of the year if a new agreement were not approved.
"I think the contract is more important to De Beers than De Beers is to Russia," Bychkov said.
He called for a stronger role by the government in the rough diamond market.
